problem: Recent studies reveal two intriguing phenomena in large language models—attention sinks and massive activations—but their co-emergence and interaction remain poorly understood.
approach: Through theoretical analysis and empirical evidence, the authors investigate how massive activations and attention sinks jointly prevent excessive token mixing in self-attention, showing that sinks suppress non-sink mixing while activations suppress mixing between sink and non-sink tokens.
contribution: Provides a mechanistic perspective on how massive activations and attention sinks interact under normalization and self-attention layers, offering new insights into their functional roles in Transformers.

problem: LiDAR point cloud compression requires learned entropy modeling for high-resolution sensors, but faces prohibitive decoding latency from causal multi-stage context modeling and rigid performance-latency trade-offs.
approach: PACE reformulates ancestral context aggregation as non-causal and confines causality to a lightweight, stage-scalable predictor, eliminating repetitive backbone executions and supporting seamless adaptation across diverse performance-latency constraints.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art compression efficiency with notable BD-BR savings and reduces decoding latency by over 90% in autoregressive mode.

problem: Policies trained on standard simplifications of spreading processes (mean-field ODEs, Markovian dynamics) suffer severe performance degradation at deployment on realistic stochastic dynamics.
approach: Introduces the Stratified Mean-Field Observer to partition nodes by influence tier at O(N) cost while preserving hub dynamics, and employs distributional RL via Truncated Quantile Critics to improve risk-aware control of bimodal cascades.
contribution: Achieves 59× improvement over Markovian baselines and demonstrates robust zero-shot transfer to real-world social networks (Facebook, Twitter, YouTube).

problem: Hierarchical policies in offline goal-conditioned RL assume that goal representations preserving information sufficient for value estimation are adequate for action learning, but this assumption can fail.
approach: Introduces an information-theoretic framework defining action sufficiency as a condition on goal representations necessary for optimal action selection, and proposes Curvilinear Demonstration Selection to order demonstrations by difficulty and conceptual progression.
contribution: Demonstrates that action-sufficient representations consistently outperform value-derived representations, with up to 5.42 percentage-point gain on math tasks with 64 demonstrations.

problem: Parameter-based knowledge editing methods for LLMs overlook fundamental theoretical limitations and are rarely evaluated under realistic practice-oriented settings, often causing reasoning collapse.
approach: Presents theoretical analysis based on the dimensional Collapse Hypothesis explaining how localized parameter edits propagate along fragile directions in representation space, combined with comprehensive empirical evaluation varying knowledge complexity and number of edits.
contribution: Shows parameter-based editing methods consistently damage core LLM capabilities, while a simple retrieval-based baseline achieves consistently stronger performance across all evaluated conditions.

problem: Learning optimal linear contracts from data in the offline setting where the principal designs contracts to maximize expected utility remains theoretically unresolved.
approach: Analyzes the Empirical Utility Maximization (EUM) algorithm, proving it yields an ε-approximation of the optimal linear contract with O(ln(1/δ) / ε²) samples and establishes uniform convergence guarantees.
contribution: Matches a lower bound from Dütting et al. (2025) up to constant factors, proving optimality and establishing uniform convergence with the same optimal sample complexity.

problem: LLM-based molecule generation faces dense and entangled representations that impede precise control over generation of molecules with bespoke substructures or properties.
approach: Proposes Sparse Representation Editing (SpaRE), an interpretability-driven framework that learns an overcomplete sparse feature space disentangling LLM representations into latent features corresponding to chemically meaningful concepts, enabling direct manipulation for local and global control.
contribution: Generates chemically desirable molecules under complex constraints in real-world scenarios while offering mechanistic insights for quantitative structure-property analysis.

problem: Diffusion LLMs face an accuracy-parallelism trade-off: existing methods target either efficiency or accuracy, preventing realization of benefits like parallel decoding and random-order generation in practice.
approach: Proposes d3LLM with pseudo-trajectory distillation to teach the model which tokens can be decoded confidently at early steps and entropy-based multi-block decoding with KV-cache refresh to maintain accuracy during parallel inference.
contribution: Achieves up to 10× speedup over vanilla LLaDA/Dream and 5× speedup over AR models without significant accuracy drop.

problem: Many-shot in-context learning on reasoning tasks remains poorly understood, with prior scaling studies focusing mainly on non-reasoning tasks.
approach: Analyzes many-shot CoT-ICL across non-reasoning and reasoning tasks, interpreting it as in-context test-time learning guided by principles that demonstrations should be easy to understand and ordered for conceptual progression.
contribution: Proposes Curvilinear Demonstration Selection yielding up to 5.42 percentage-point gain on math tasks with 64 demonstrations, reframing the long context window as a structured curriculum.

problem: Classical uniformly-bounded-variance analysis breaks down for subsampling regimes common in practice, even for finite-sum objectives on unbounded domains.
approach: Studies momentum Linear Minimization Oracle (LMO) methods under expected smoothness (ABC condition) capturing common sampling schemes, introducing a self-bounding closure handling history-coupling induced by momentum.
contribution: Establishes unified nonconvex convergence theory recovering known bounded-variance results as a special case and derives explicit batch-size scaling laws predicting optimal momentum-batch trade-offs.

problem: Natural Language Querying for Time Series Databases struggles with continuous morphological intents like shapes or anomalies, while time series models handle ultra-long histories poorly.
approach: Proposes Sonar-TS, a neuro-symbolic framework using a 'Search-Then-Verify' pipeline: an SQL-based feature index 'pings' candidate windows, followed by generated Python programs to verify against raw signals.
contribution: Introduces NLQTSBench, the first large-scale benchmark for NLQ over TSDB-scale histories, demonstrating Sonar-TS effectively navigates complex temporal queries.

problem: Zeroth-Order optimization faces a stark trade-off: standard finite differences are sample-inefficient while randomized methods suffer from high variance, hindering practical deployment.
approach: Proposes Coherent Coordinate Descent (CoCD), a deterministic ZO optimizer treating historical stale gradients as computational assets via gradient coherence, maintaining global descent directions with O(1) query complexity per step.
contribution: Demonstrates CoCD significantly outperforms Block Cyclic Coordinate Descent and randomized ZO methods on MLP, CNN, and ResNet architectures up to 270k parameters.

problem: Existing ternarization methods for LLM compression keep activations in high precision due to heavy-tailed distributions, fundamentally limiting end-to-end inference acceleration.
approach: Proposes TWLA, a post-training quantization framework combining E2M-ATQ for layer-output error minimization, KOTMS for ternary-friendly distribution shaping, and ILA-AMP for layer-wise activation bit allocation.
contribution: Achieves 1.58-bit weight compression and 4-bit activation quantization (W1.58A4 configuration) while maintaining high accuracy.

problem: Monitoring behavioral dynamics in black-box multi-agent systems lacks principled frameworks, making it difficult to detect when agents change behavior over time.
approach: Introduces Temporal Data Kernel Perspective Space (TDKPS) jointly embedding agents across time and proposes novel hypothesis tests for detecting behavioral change at agent- and group-level via black-box queries.
contribution: Demonstrates TDKPS detects changes that correlate sensitively, specifically, and significantly with real exogenous events, establishing the first principled framework for monitoring behavioral dynamics.

problem: Strong theoretical inapproximability results for NP-hard problems like correlation clustering pessimistically assume worst-case inputs, preventing assessment of algorithm quality on real-world datasets.
approach: Develops efficient algorithms computing lower bounds on optimal solutions via multiplicative weights update framework near-linear time on sparse graphs, yielding instance-specific approximation ratios.
contribution: Certifies that state-of-the-art heuristics achieve almost optimal approximation ratios of 0.94 for agreement and 1.97 for disagreement version on correlation clustering averaged over 7 real-world datasets.

problem: Deep learning models with accurate predictions often learn latent representations that are temporally disordered lacking continuity, a phenomenon termed Latent Chaos caused by minimizing point-wise errors on noisy partially observed data.
approach: Proposes Latent Time Series Forecasting (LatentTSF) shifting forecasting from observation regression to latent state prediction via an AutoEncoder, enabling focus on structured temporal dynamics.
contribution: Effectively mitigates latent chaos yielding consistent improvements in both forecasting accuracy and representation quality with information-theoretic justification.

problem: Detecting hallucinations in LLMs under zero-source constraint—where no model internals or external references are available—remains challenging.
approach: Proposes HCPD emulating multi-faceted reasoning of human evaluators via a Human-like Criteria Probing mechanism in which an LLM agent adaptively decomposes judgment into weighted interpretable criteria and aggregates scores.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in zero-source hallucination detection while offering full interpretability.

problem: Relational Deep Learning faces a fundamental tension: Transformers' quadratic complexity prohibits large contexts relational data demands while GNNs sacrifice global context for efficiency.
approach: Introduces Ramba, a selective state-space model featuring Topology-Aware Linearization processing cells via global columnar serialization at O(L) complexity and Schema Dynamic Gating modulating state transitions based on semantic alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with linear scalability across diverse relational benchmarks.

problem: Existing LLM IP verification methods rely on invasive watermarking degrading model utility or superficial behavioral signatures disrupted by fine-tuning and model merging.
approach: Proposes CircuitPrint, a non-invasive IP fingerprinting framework leveraging stable internal computational circuits of LLMs as persistent backbones across model derivatives, identifying mechanistically essential supernodes.
contribution: Substantially outperforms existing baselines while remaining robust under aggressive fine-tuning and model merging without altering model parameters.

problem: Alignment strategies aiming to restrict harmful behavior in LLMs can be circumvented through carefully designed adversarial prompts.
approach: Introduces a game-theoretic framework formalizing a game between an attacker hiding intent via compositional skills and a defender, designing theoretically optimal attack and defense strategies.
contribution: Shows attacker has inherent advantages and derives provably optimal defense strategy, with empirical evaluation demonstrating stronger attack performance than existing adversarial prompting approaches.

problem: How planning decisions in self-evolving LLM agents for CUDA kernel generation attribute and combine heterogeneous feedback signals remains opaque.
approach: Introduces CUDAnalyst, a unified analysis layer enabling controlled generation-level attribution of planning decisions to feedback components via trajectory freezing and selective feedback injection.
contribution: Shows explicit planning is beneficial only when feedback is aligned and effective planning emerges from structured multi-feedback interactions, with partial transfer from stronger to weaker reasoning models.

problem: Efficiently removing undesirable visual concepts from image generative models without degrading output quality remains challenging.
approach: Introduces concept removal by replacing the internal bottleneck layer in frontier diffusion and autoregressive models with a transcoder trained to structure activations into distinct features, enabling selective disabling of concept-specific signals.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art concept removal across modern diffusion and autoregressive models (SD3.5, Flux, Infinity) while maintaining visual generation quality and supporting sequential removal.

problem: Precise alignment of hyperspectral and multispectral images for fusion requires handling complex non-rigid deformations, yet existing methods suffer from inter-task error accumulation or neglect geometric distortions.
approach: Proposes Structure-Aware Riemannian Flow Matching (SA-RFM) reformulating registration as dynamic optimal transport on a structure-induced Riemannian manifold via conditional flow matching with Riemannian objectives.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority across four datasets with joint registration and fusion handling complex non-rigid deformations through geometry-informed framework.

problem: The phenomenon that on-policy preference learning algorithms outperform offline counterparts lacks rigorous theoretical explanation.
approach: Analyzes how the sampling policy's coverage evolves throughout on-policy training, proposing the coverage improvement principle: with sufficient batch size each update moves into a region with uniformly better coverage.
contribution: Proves on-policy DPO converges exponentially in iterations for batch size exceeding a generalized coverage threshold and shows faster minimax rate than offline counterparts, with sample complexity separation.

problem: Optimization dynamics of zeroth-order methods in deep learning remain underexplored, lacking stability characterizations comparable to first-order methods.
approach: Provides an explicit step size condition capturing mean-square linear stability of ZO methods based on two-point estimators, revealing dependence on full Hessian spectrum and deriving tractable bounds using largest eigenvalue and trace.
contribution: Finds ZO methods operate at the edge of stability with implicit regularization specific to ZO where large step sizes regularize Hessian trace rather than top eigenvalue.

problem: In-context reinforcement learning via Decision-Pretrained Transformers remains vulnerable to reward poisoning attacks, limiting practical deployment.
approach: Proposes Adversarially Trained DPT (AT-DPT) simultaneously training a population of attackers to poison environment rewards and a DPT model to infer optimal actions from poisoned data.
contribution: Significantly outperforms robust baselines in bandit settings under learned attackers and generalizes to complex environments including adaptive attackers and MDPs.

problem: Existing Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning methods like LoRA originally tailored for autoregressive models rely on static parameters agnostic to noise level in diffusion models.
approach: Proposes NaRA introducing a low-rank core matrix generated by a lightweight hypernetwork conditioned on noise level, enabling updates to vary continuously along the diffusion process with negligible overhead.
contribution: Provides theoretical justification and empirically demonstrates consistent improvements over noise-agnostic baselines across commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation benchmarks.

problem: Training self-supervised foundation models for functional MRI and scaling them requires appropriate representations and evaluation methods.
approach: Introduces CortexMAE trained using masked autoencoder on 2.1K hours of fMRI data with cortical flat map projection converting 3D volumes to 2D maps and releases Brainmarks evaluation suite.
contribution: Observes strict power law scaling for fMRI, demonstrates CortexMAE outperforms prior models on cognitive state decoding by large margin though null results on trait prediction versus functional connectivity baseline.

problem: Foundation flow-matching models promise universal priors for solving inverse problems but trail behind domain-specific and untrained priors.
approach: Introduces FMPlug combining instance-guided time-dependent warm-start strategy with sharp Gaussianity regularization, adding problem-specific guidance while preserving Gaussian structures.
contribution: Superior experimental results on simple image restoration and scientific inverse problems demonstrate effectiveness of FMPlug making foundation FM models practical reusable priors.

problem: Training generative models with heterogeneous data sources (on-policy and off-policy) requires loss functions maintaining the same global minimizer across both regimes.
approach: Demonstrates that mean square error construction extends to f-divergences, yielding a family of losses whose on-policy gradients match f-divergence objectives while maintaining the same global minimizer off-policy.
contribution: Applies f-trajectory balance to GFlowNets, generative models, and LLM tuning, showing models retain predicted properties and can adapt to off-policy data.

problem: Federated learning suffers from degraded generalization under global class imbalance and cross-client data heterogeneity, with mismatch between local and global imbalances exacerbating performance.
approach: Proposes FedReLa, a data-level approach using feature-dependent label re-allocator to correct biased global decision boundaries without requiring global class distribution knowledge.
contribution: Significantly improves minority class accuracy and overall accuracy on stepwise-imbalanced and long-tailed datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art without additional communication overhead.

problem: Comparing autoregressive (AR) and Masked Diffusion Model (MDM) paradigms is confounded by differing architectures, obscuring true algorithmic and efficiency trade-offs.
approach: Evaluates MDMs within decoder-only framework to equitably compare with standard AR methods and investigates MDM architectural impacts on computational efficiency.
contribution: Shows decoder-only MDMs despite larger modeling space achieve significant inference speedups (~25×) and comparable perplexity with temperature annealing, offering path to reduced inference compute.

problem: Speculative decoding with binary accept/recompute decisions wastes computational resources on tokens that could be verified by smaller models.
approach: Proposes VIA-SD, a multi-tier framework using routed slim-verifier for tokens requiring moderate verification resources, hierarchically processing draft tokens via direct acceptance, slim-verifier regeneration, or full-model verification.
contribution: Reduces rejection rates by 0.10–0.22 and delivers 10–20% speedups over strong SD baselines while achieving 2.5–3× acceleration over non-drafting decoding.

problem: Offline preference-based RL typically follows a two-stage pipeline learning rewards then performing offline RL, potentially discarding useful reward-free signal.
approach: Revisits offline PbRL through reward-free representation learning (RFRL) lens, proposing a framework learning latent successor-measure representations from unlabeled data before contrastive search and fine-tuning with preference data.
contribution: Achieves superior preference efficiency over offline PbRL baselines, first connecting RFRL with PbRL for feedback-efficient solution.

problem: Predicting long-horizon trajectories of biological dynamical systems remains challenging due to substantial system heterogeneity, with most approaches being system-specific.
approach: Creates benchmark of over 1,000 ODE-based systems biology models and proposes regime-aware framework introducing structured initial states derived from biological regime priors into conditional flow matching.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy (31% MAE reduction), well-calibrated uncertainty (17% CRPS improvement), and efficient long-horizon inference across benchmark.

problem: Federated learning under statistical heterogeneity suffers from flatness discrepancy where local flatness does not transfer to global model due to misaligned loss landscapes.
approach: Proposes FedScar maintaining history-accumulated geometric bias capturing persistent curvature skew across clients with variance-aware injection steering updates toward globally flat regions.
contribution: Consistently reduces flatness discrepancy and improves generalization under severe heterogeneity over state-of-the-art without additional communication overhead.

problem: Many modern generative models minimize different divergences and rely on different principles, making unified analysis difficult.
approach: Presents unified theoretical framework for generative modeling based on Wasserstein gradient flows, showing broad class of existing methods derive as instances of parametric JKO schemes for f-divergence objectives.
contribution: Establishes equivalences between recently proposed algorithms and extends framework beyond f-divergences to Integral Probability Metrics and squared Maximum Mean Discrepancy.

problem: Understanding which historical events drive Temporal Graph Network predictions remains challenging as existing explanation methods overlook the memory module.
approach: Attributes TGN predictions through topology attribution tree capturing influence of neighbors and memory vectors, then memory backtracking tree quantifying how historical events shape memory vectors.
contribution: Provides faithful explanations outperforming state-of-the-art baselines across nine temporal graph datasets spanning node prediction, link prediction, and graph classification.

problem: Vision-Language Models like CLIP underperform on multi-label recognition where multiple objects co-exist because the CLS token is insufficient to encode diverse targets with varying scales.
approach: Presents PIAA formulating prediction as Patch-level Inference followed by Adaptive Aggregation, with training-free pipeline enhancing patch-wise predictions and introducing adaptive aggregation module.
contribution: Achieves strong improvements with minimal computation exceeding 6% mAP gain on NUS-WIDE benchmark over baselines, fully training-free requiring no gradient updates.

problem: Learning operators of physical field equations on geometric meshes faces spectral interference from unlearnable topological degrees of freedom.
approach: Reveals that Hodge orthogonality fundamentally resolves spectral interference and derives principled operator-level decomposition via Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian architecture with Hodge Spectral Duality inductive bias.
contribution: Achieves superior accuracy and efficiency on geometric graphs with enhanced fidelity to physical invariants using discrete differential forms and orthogonal auxiliary space.
